purpose: Stabilize authoritative movement and durable persistence, expose split server/client launch commands, and preserve diagnostic logs.
root_causes: The graphical client and dedicated server simulated different movement models concurrently, causing authoritative rollback/rubber-banding.
High-frequency movement COMMAND_RESULT messages accumulated on the client and movement mutations forced synchronous durable checkpoints.
Double-precision movement coordinates changed their JSON numeric representation across persistence roundtrip, invalidating nested durable checksums and forcing server fail-stop.
Item-command rejection reasons and stale READY files were not visible enough for manual diagnosis.
fixes: Client sends MOVEMENT_INTENT only and renders authoritative snapshots with target smoothing; local CharacterBody prediction is disabled.
Movement results are asynchronous and discarded after accounting; blocking command buffers stay bounded.
Movement checkpoints are batched at a 1500 ms interval and a following durable item command includes the latest movement state.
All durable checksum boundaries bind to the canonical JSON-roundtripped representation, including checkpoint, registry, ownership, Item Graph, replay and outbox payloads.
Dedicated server, client A and client B have independent PowerShell launch commands, profiles, process descriptors and log files.
Debug clients remain open after disconnect, reject stale server process descriptors, and expose human-readable item rejection messages.

runtime_validation.powershell_execution: NOT_RUN_ON_LINUX; independent Windows launcher acceptance required
